According to [budget_2026_27_memorandum_finance_bill.pdf, p.42], sub-section (2) of section 270AA provides that an assessee shall file an application within one month from the end of the month in which the assessment order has been received by him. 

However, the specific conditions for applying for immunity from penalty under section 270A are not mentioned in [budget_2026_27_memorandum_finance_bill.pdf, p.42]. 

But, according to [budget_2026_27_finance_bill.pdf, p.179-180], it is proposed to amend the section 270AA so as to extend such immunity to cases where penalty is initiated for under-reporting of income in consequence of misreporting, on payment of the tax and interest payable as per the order of assessment under sub-section (3) of section 143 or reassessment under section 147, along with additional income-tax amounting to one hundred per cent. of the aggregate of such tax payable.

However, the exact conditions for applying for immunity from penalty under section 270A are not mentioned in [budget_2026_27_finance_bill.pdf, p.179-180] either.

But, according to [budget_2026_27_finance_bill.pdf, p.88], sub-section (1) of section 440 (which is the same as section 270AA) provides that an assessee may make an application to the Assessing Officer to grant waiver of penalty levied under section 439 and immunity from initiation of proceedings under section 478 or 479 on fulfilment of the following conditions: 

(a) the tax and interest payable as per the order of assessment under section 270(10) or reassessment under section 279, has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand;

(b) where penalty has been levied under the circumstances referred to in section 439(11)(a) to (f), additional income-tax amounting to 100% of the amount of tax payable on under-reported income has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand, in lieu of such penalty;

(c) where penalty has been levied under the circumstances referred to in section 439(11)(g), additional income-tax amounting to 120% of the amount of tax payable on under-reported income has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand, in lieu of such penalty; and

(d) no appeal has been filed against the order of assessment or reassessment and levy of penalty referred to in clause (a), (b) and (c).

Therefore, according to [budget_2026_27_finance_bill.pdf, p.88], the conditions for applying for immunity from penalty under section 270A are:

* The tax and interest payable as per the order of assessment under section 270(10) or reassessment under section 279, has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand.
* Where penalty has been levied under the circumstances referred to in section 439(11)(a) to (f), additional income-tax amounting to 100% of the amount of tax payable on under-reported income has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand, in lieu of such penalty.
* Where penalty has been levied under the circumstances referred to in section 439(11)(g), additional income-tax amounting to 120% of the amount of tax payable on under-reported income has been paid within the period specified in the notice of demand, in lieu of such penalty.
* No appeal has been filed against the order of assessment or reassessment and levy of penalty referred to in clause (a), (b) and (c).
expected: The assessee applies to the Assessing Officer; conditions include (a) the tax and interest payable under the assessment order (section 143(3)) or reassessment (section 147) has been paid within the period in the notice of demand, plus the further conditions in section 270AA(1).

|(Amount in Rs crore).||Profit/loss||Absolute value of profit/loss after tax||Average of absolute|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|(Amount in Rs. crore)||after tax|value of profit/loss|
|(Amount in Rs. crore)||after tax for the 3years|

|FY 2021-22|50|50|50|50|50|50|50|
|FY 2022-23|(20)|(20)|(20)|20|20|20|20|

The average absolute value of profit or loss after tax is calculated by adding the absolute values of profit/loss for each year and dividing by 3. In this case, the average is (20+50+20) / 3 = 30.

| FY 2020-21 | FY 2021-22 | FY 2022-23 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profit/Loss | 20 | 50 | 20 |
| Absolute value of profit/loss after tax | 20 | 50 | 20 |
| Average of absolute value of profit/loss | (20+50+20) / 3 = 30 |
expected: Absolute values are averaged regardless of sign: (20 + 50 + 20) / 3 = Rs 30 crore.
